literal: My lord before do not stand, O enemies! Many, my lord before having stood, [are] those who stood [as] stone.
translation: O enemies, do not stand against my lord! Many who stood before him are now standing as memorial stones.
modern: பகைவர்களே! என் தலைவனுக்கு முன்னே போரிட நிற்காதீர்கள். அவனுக்கு முன் எதிர்த்து நின்ற பலர் இப்போது நடுகல்லாக நிற்கிறார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet is spoken by a warrior warning the enemy forces about his commander's fierce prowess in battle. The word 'என்னை' (eṉṉai) here is formed from 'என்' (my) and 'ஐ' (lord or master), meaning 'my commander', rather than the accusative pronoun 'me'. The warrior warns that many who previously dared to stand against his lord are now standing as 'கல்' (kal), referring to the hero stones erected for the dead. It vividly conveys the lethal certainty of facing this great warrior.
